book.title: The Gevher Nesibe Hospital and Medical School

pages.title: A Hospital Ahead of Its Time
pages.content:
The Gevher Nesibe Complex in Kayseri is the oldest surviving Anatolian Seljuk hospital, and the world’s first example of a hospital and a medical school built together as one complex. The systematic medical training established in Anatolia in the 13th century, which combined theoretical education with clinical training at the bedside, did not appear in Europe until the 16th and 17th centuries. Furthermore, the Imperial Medical School (Mekteb-i Tıbbiyye-i Adliyye-i Şâhâne), established by Sultan Mahmud II, was opened more than 600 years after the Kayseri Medical School.

At the time the Gevher Nesibe Complex was established, Konya served as the capital of the Seljuk Sultanate, while Kayseri was regarded as a second capital and was known as ‘Makarr-ı Ulemâ’ (the center of scholars).

The building complex, which today functions as the Museum of the Seljuk Civilization, was constructed by the Anatolian Seljuk ruler Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev I in honor of his sister, Gevher Nesibe Sultan.

exercises.title: Ahead of Its Time
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the chapter supports.
exercises.question: Why is the complex described as ahead of its time?
options: It combined theoretical education with clinical training centuries before Europe did.
It was the largest hospital of the Seljuk Sultanate.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “The systematic medical training established in Anatolia in the 13th century, which combined theoretical education with clinical training at the bedside, did not appear in Europe until the 16th and 17th centuries.”

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: Established by …
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose what the phrase in bold quotes does.
languageFocusExercises.question: “The Imperial Medical School, ‘established by Sultan Mahmud II’, was opened more than 600 years after the Kayseri Medical School.” What does the phrase do?

It is the main verb of the sentence.
It shows the purpose of the school.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Established by Sultan Mahmud II” = “which was established by Sultan Mahmud II”. A past participle phrase can follow a noun and work like a passive relative clause. The main verb is “was opened”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Not … Until, While, Regarded As
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 1.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Not … until + time” means the event started only at that time. “While” joins two contrasting facts in one sentence. “Be regarded as” = be thought of as.

feedback.correct: Well done. Until, while, regarded.
feedback.incorrect: Check the time word, the contrast linker and the passive verb.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Ahead of Its Time
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write a paragraph of five to six sentences about an invention or idea that was ahead of its time.

In many other places, it was not until much later that such libraries became common. While most books were very expensive, these libraries made knowledge free to everyone. This idea was clearly ahead of its time. Today, public libraries still serve as places where anyone can learn.”

pages.title: A Princess and a Commander
pages.content: Gevher Nesibe Sultan was the daughter of Kılıçarslan II (d. 1192) and also the sister of Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev I (d. 1211). According to legend, when Gevher Nesibe was a young girl, she fell in love with the commander of the Seljuk Cavalry Regiment. However, her elder brother, Sultan Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev I, opposed the relationship and did not allow them to marry. Instead, he wanted his younger sister to marry a courtier. When her brother informed her of this decision, Gevher Nesibe rejected it. To separate them, Sultan Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev I sent the commander away to war. Following the commander’s martyrdom, Gevher Nesibe Sultan’s intense grief weakened her, eventually causing her to contract tuberculosis. Due to the lack of a proper medical facility in Kayseri, she tragically died of the disease at a young age. When she was on her deathbed, Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev I apologized to her and asked for her final wish.

exercises.title: The Legend in Order
exercises.instructions: Put the events of the legend in the order the chapter tells them.

Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev I opposed the relationship.

The commander was sent away to war.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 2 tells the legend as a chain: love, opposition, refusal, war, grief and illness.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: Following the Commander’s Martyrdom
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose what the -ing phrase at the end does.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Gevher Nesibe Sultan’s intense grief weakened her, eventually causing her to contract tuberculosis.” What does “causing her to contract tuberculosis” express?

languageFocusExercises.explanation: A comma + -ing clause after the main clause can express a result: the grief weakened her, and as a result she contracted tuberculosis. “Eventually” shows that it took some time.

Today, people still drink from it, remembering his kindness.”

pages.title: The Last Wish
pages.content:
As the legend goes, Gevher Nesibe Sultan made a final request in her last days:

“I have fallen ill with an incurable disease, and there is no hope of recovery. No physician has been able to find a cure for my illness, and I am now on my way to the afterlife. Please use my wealth to establish a hospital in my memory. Let this hospital heal the sick, while also searching for cures to untreatable diseases. Let renowned physicians and surgeons be trained here. Let no one pay a single dirham (penny). Let this place stand as a charity in my name.” She then donated her entire fortune to this cause.

The process of becoming healthy again.
Impossible to treat with medicine.
Help given free to people in need.
All the money and property someone has.
An aim that people support or work for.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: Incurable, Untreatable
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose what the prefixes in- and un- do.
languageFocusExercises.question: “I have fallen ill with an incurable disease … while also searching for cures to untreatable diseases.” What do in- and un- do?
options: They give the adjective the opposite meaning: not able to be cured or treated.
They make the adjective stronger: very curable.
They change the adjective into a verb.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: In- and un- are negative prefixes. Curable means “able to be cured”, so incurable means “not able to be cured”. Treatable becomes untreatable. The suffix -able means “can be …”.

feedback.correct: Correct. They make the meaning negative.
feedback.incorrect: Remove the prefix. What is left?

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 3.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

Let no one [choice] a single dirham.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Let + object + base verb” (or + be + past participle for a passive) expresses a solemn wish. “Has been able to” is the present perfect of can: from the past until now.

pages.title: The Twin Madrasas
pages.content: To fulfill his sister’s will, Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev built a madrasa (Gıyâsiye Medresesi), and then a hospital (Şifâiye). Construction of the hospital was completed in two years. Gevher Nesibe Sultan was buried in her tomb inside the madrasa. Because the two buildings are next to one another, they are also known among the people as the ‘Twin Madrasas.’ According to the inscription on the main gate of the Dârüşşifâ, the construction date is 1205–1206.

vocabulary.definition: A large stone grave, often inside a building.

languageFocusExercises.title: Notice: To Fulfill His Sister’s Will
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose what “To fulfill his sister’s will” tells us.
languageFocusExercises.question: “To fulfill his sister’s will, Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev built a madrasa, and then a hospital.” What does the first phrase tell us?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A to-infinitive at the beginning of a sentence gives the purpose of the main action. It answers the question “Why?”.

feedback.correct: Correct. It gives his purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Which question does the phrase answer: why, when or where?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build: Passives and Be Known As
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: Construction of the hospital [choice] in two years.
Gevher Nesibe Sultan [choice] in her tomb inside the madrasa.
They are also known among the people [choice] the ‘Twin Madrasas.’

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The passive (was + past participle) focuses on the result when the doer is obvious. “Be known as + name” gives the name people use.

feedback.correct: Well done. Was completed, was buried, as.
feedback.incorrect: Is the subject doing the action or receiving it?

languageFocusExercises.explanation: A reason clause can come first or second. “In order to” is a more formal purpose form. “It took + time + to + verb” is another way to express duration.

languageFocusExercises.question: Who built it, and why do people call it that?

People call it this because it is in the center of the town and full of trees. Today, families meet there every weekend.”

pages.title: Learning Beside the Patients
pages.content: In the 13th century, education at this medical institution combined theory at the Gıyâsiye and practical training at the Şifâiye. Excavations suggest that the buildings were heated from below using steam from a nearby bathhouse. Students likely stayed in small rooms within the complex. During the summer, classes were held in the large courtyards, which were also used to examine outpatients. Although this is not certain, the staff is generally believed to have included a chief physician with his assistants, at least two internists, two surgeons, and a pharmacist. This staff was similar to that of the Keykâvus Dârüşşifâ in Sivas.

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose what the writer is doing.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Although this is not certain, the staff is generally believed to have included a chief physician with his assistants …” What is the writer doing?
options: reporting a common view about the past without claiming it is proven
giving a fact from an official document

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Be believed to have + past participle” reports what people generally think about the past. “Although this is not certain” makes the writer’s caution clear.

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 5.

pages.title: Great Teachers and Books
pages.content: Some notable physicians and scholars worked and taught there in both the Seljuk and Ottoman periods. Some of them were Abdüllatîf al-Baghdadî, Ekmeleddin al-Nahcuvânî (Mevlânâ’s close friend and personal physician), Sadreddin Konevî, Kutbüddin al-Shirazi, Ali Sivasi, Inayetullah (the mufti of Kayseri), and Fahri Pasha, the Janissary Agha. Among them, Abdüllatîf al-Baghdadî (d. 1231) was a versatile scholar and philosopher. Kutbüddin al-Shirazi (d. 1311), nicknamed ‘kehhâl’ (the ophthalmologist), wrote a commentary on Ibn Sînâ’s al-Qanun fi’l-Tibb. At the Gıyâsiye, these scholars lectured on philosophy, religious sciences, Arabic, Persian, anatomy, and physiology. They taught the most important medical texts of the era, including the works of Abu Bakr al-Razi and Ibn Sînâ. They also taught ancient Greek and Roman sources, particularly Arabic translations of Hippocrates and Galen. Clinical training, on the other hand, took place at patients’ bedsides in the Şifâiye Hospital.

pages.title: Inside the Buildings
pages.content:
The two structures are connected by a corridor. Each has an enclosed courtyard with a pool, as well as rooms of different sizes. All the doors are small and open onto covered walkways. None of the rooms have fireplaces or chimneys. No kitchen-like space was found, which suggests that meals were brought in from an outdoor kitchen.

The Gevher Nesibe Dârüşşifâ had three operating rooms, and two surgeons were on staff. Small windows at the top of the operating rooms provided dim lighting, which made it easier to control the light during operations. It is believed that minor surgeries and cataract operations were performed here.

pages.title: Medical Education at the Dârüşşifâ
pages.content:
The educational method of the era was based on the master-apprentice model. Students who graduated successfully received an icâzet (diploma). The document listed the names of both the instructors and their teachers in a hierarchical order. Students who took classes there were known as ‘dânişmend.’

Education at the Dârüşşifâ was essentially divided into two parts. The first stage consisted of courses in mathematics, astronomy, physics, grammar, philosophy, and medicine. Together, these courses were known as ‘dârü’l-ilim’. In the second stage, Islamic sciences were taught. Treatment methods were based on the recommendations of scientists such as Bîrûnî and Ibn Sînâ (known as Avicenna in the West), who were influential figures of the time. Medicines were prepared according to the prescriptions of the era’s leading physicians. Sources also indicate that bedside training sessions were held. According to the most recent documents available, the Dârüşşifâ continued to operate until the early 1900s.

pages.title: Music Therapy at the Dârüşşifâ
pages.content: In his work Kitâbü’ş-Şifâ, Ibn Sînâ states that one of the best ways to treat a patient is by strengthening their mental and spiritual power, giving them courage through loved ones, and using the healing power of music. Al-Razi noted that melancholic patients should be treated with music. Meanwhile, Fârâbî examined how different musical modes (makams) affect the human soul. He classified these modes into categories based on the emotions they evoke, such as joy, fear, comfort, and a sense of infinity. Furthermore, Fârâbî explained which mode is most effective at specific times of the day. In this context, it is clear that music therapy was also practiced at the Gevher Nesibe Dârüşşifâ.

pages.title: A Legacy That Lives On
pages.content:
Throughout history, there have been many examples of hospitals and medical schools, but none are known to have combined both into a single structure quite like the Gevher Nesibe Dârüşşifâ. Compared to Salerno, Bologna, and Paris, which are historically recognized as the pioneering universities of medical education, the Gevher Nesibe Dârüşşifâ was more advanced in many aspects. This medical center (dârüşşifâ) and educational madrasa emerged directly from centuries of accumulated knowledge. They represent the great achievements of scholars in the Islamic world who thrived during the 9th, 10th, and 11th centuries.

Gevher Nesibe Sultan never married the love of her life, but she became the sultan of people’s hearts, living on in their memory long after her passing.

Modern and highly developed.

languageFocusExercises.question: What did they achieve, and why does it still matter?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “The old public library in my town was founded by a group of teachers many years ago. Few buildings of that time are known to have survived in our area. Compared to modern libraries, it is small and simple. However, it represents an important idea: knowledge should be free for everyone. This idea emerged from the hard work of people who loved reading. Thousands of students have studied there, and many of them now work as teachers and doctors. The library still serves the town, inspiring new generations of readers.”

feedback.correct: Check: a careful claim, compared to, represent and a participle clause of result.

Compare with others using compared to.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the language of the whole book.

exercises.title: Notice: Fact, Belief or Legend?
exercises.instructions: Sort the sentences: does the writer present them as fact, careful belief or legend?
exercises.question: How does the writer signal certainty?

items: Construction of the hospital was completed in two years.
The bathhouse is covered by a dome.
Students likely stayed in small rooms within the complex.
It is believed that minor surgeries and cataract operations were performed here.
According to legend, when Gevher Nesibe was a young girl, she fell in love with the commander.

Fact: Construction of the hospital was completed in two years.
The bathhouse is covered by a dome.
Careful belief: Students likely stayed in small rooms within the complex.
It is believed that minor surgeries and cataract operations were performed here.
Legend: According to legend, when Gevher Nesibe was a young girl, she fell in love with the commander.

exercises.explanation: Throughout the book, the writer signals stance: plain statements for facts, likely / believed / suggest for careful beliefs, and According to legend / As the legend goes for legends.

feedback.correct: Good. You read the writer’s stance.
feedback.incorrect: Look for likely, believed and legend.

exercises.title: Notice: Participle Clauses
exercises.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the one where the -ing clause shows a result.
exercises.question: Which -ing clause shows a result?
options: Her grief weakened her, eventually causing her to contract tuberculosis.
Following the commander’s martyrdom, she was very sad.
One of the best ways to treat a patient is by using the healing power of music.
exercises.explanation: After a main clause, “…, causing …” shows a result. “Following + noun” gives time; “by + -ing” gives a method.

feedback.correct: Correct. Causing … shows a result.
feedback.incorrect: Which -ing form comes after a comma at the end?

exercises.title: Notice: Sentential Which
exercises.instructions: Read the statement. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: In “No kitchen-like space was found, which suggests that …”, which refers to the whole idea before it.
exercises.explanation: After a comma, which can refer to a whole clause. Here the fact that no kitchen was found is the evidence.

feedback.correct: Correct. Which refers to the whole clause.
feedback.incorrect: What suggests something: the space, or the fact that none was found?

exercises.title: Build: Linking Ideas
exercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: How does the book link ideas?
exercises.fillBlanksText: [blank] the lack of a proper medical facility, she died young. [blank] his sister’s will, the Sultan built a madrasa and a hospital. Clinical training, [blank], took place at patients’ bedsides.
exercises.explanation: “Due to + noun phrase” gives a reason. “To + verb” at the start gives a purpose. “On the other hand” gives a contrast.

feedback.correct: Well done. Due to, To fulfill, on the other hand.
feedback.incorrect: Is each gap a reason, a purpose or a contrast?

exercises.title: Build: Reporting and Passive Patterns
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence.
exercises.question: Which pattern is correct?

formChoices.sentence: The staff is generally believed [choice] a pharmacist.
Melancholic patients should [choice] with music.
None are known [choice] both into a single structure.

exercises.explanation: “Be believed / known to have + past participle” refers to the past. “Should be + past participle” is a passive modal.

feedback.correct: Correct. To have included, be treated, to have combined.
feedback.incorrect: Check the perfect infinitive and the passive modal.

exercises.title: Build: Correct the Sentences
exercises.instructions: Find the mistake in each sentence and choose the correct form.
exercises.question: Which form is correct?

errorItems.sentence: Due to there was no proper hospital, she died young.
The first stage consisted in courses in mathematics and medicine.
Fârâbî examined how musical modes effect the human soul.

exercises.explanation: “Due to” needs a noun phrase; use because before a clause. “Consist of” lists parts. “Affect” is the verb; “effect” is the noun.

feedback.correct: Correct. Because there was, consisted of, affect.
feedback.incorrect: Check due to, the preposition and affect / effect.

exercises.title: Build: Say It Another Way
exercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence so that it keeps the same meaning.
exercises.question: How else can we say it?

transformItems.source: The building complex today functions as the Museum of the Seljuk Civilization.
transformItems.frame: The building complex is used [blank] the Museum of the Seljuk Civilization today.

transformItems.source: It is believed that minor surgeries were performed here.
transformItems.frame: Minor surgeries are believed to have [blank] performed here.

transformItems.source: This training did not appear in Europe until the 16th and 17th centuries.
transformItems.frame: It was not until the 16th and 17th centuries [blank] this training appeared in Europe.

exercises.explanation: “Function as” = “be used as”. “It is believed that …” = “… are believed to have been …”. “It was not until … that …” stresses the time.

feedback.correct: Well done. Same meaning, new structure.
feedback.incorrect: Use as, been and that.

exercises.title: Use: A New Context
exercises.instructions: Read about a modern teaching hospital. Fill each gap from the word bank.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s language in a new text?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Our city’s teaching hospital, [blank] in 1960, trains hundreds of doctors every year. Its method is [blank] on bedside training. Recent reports [blank] that patients recover faster there. The hospital is [blank] as one of the best in the region.
exercises.explanation: A reduced relative clause (founded in …), be based on, reports indicate that and be regarded as all come from the book. Here they describe a modern hospital.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s language in a new text.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the words around each gap.

exercises.title: Use: Check a Short Report
exercises.instructions: A student wrote about a museum visit. Find and correct each mistake.
exercises.question: What should the student change?

errorItems.sentence: The museum, which built in the 13th century, is very old.
Students who visits it learn a lot.
No kitchen was found, what suggests that meals came from outside.

exercises.explanation: Use a passive in a relative clause about a building, a plural verb after “students who”, and which (not what) for a whole clause.

feedback.correct: Correct. Which was built, visit, which.
feedback.incorrect: Check the passive, the verb agreement and the relative pronoun.

exercises.title: Use: An Institution That Serves People
exercises.instructions: Write eight to ten sentences evaluating an institution in your town that serves people.
exercises.question: What does it do, what do we know about it, and why does it matter?
exercises.explanation: Example: “The public hospital in my town, built in the 1950s, is the oldest health institution in the area. It is regarded as one of the best hospitals in the region. It is believed to have treated more than a million patients, although exact numbers are not available. Its old buildings still have high ceilings and large windows, which suggests that the builders cared about light and air. Compared to new private hospitals, it is simple, but it serves everyone. Many doctors who trained there now work all over the country. Like the Gevher Nesibe Dârüşşifâ, it represents the idea that health care is a service to the community.”

feedback.correct: Check: a reduced relative clause, a careful belief, …, which suggests that … and compared to.

discussionPrompts.question: Introduce it with a reduced relative clause.
Separate facts from careful beliefs.
Draw a conclusion with …, which suggests that.
Evaluate its legacy with compared to.
